description: Harness-capability case for `bypassCredentialTest`: the simulated user sets up a Slack credential the stage direction describes as WORKING, so the proxy sets `credentialWorks` and the harness registers the created id for connection-test bypass. This is the only variant that reproduces the real UI journey end to end — the product refuses to apply a setup card whose credential fails its test (`isCredentialComplete` returns `isCredentialTestedOk`), so without the bypass a placeholder token is a state a real user could never reach, and the agent correctly spends its closing message telling them to reconnect. With the bypass the test resolves successful, the card applies as it would with a real account, and the agent should report a clean build with no credential caveat. Sibling of credential-setup-proxy-creates-credential, which is the same flow WITHOUT the bypass and asserts the honest invalid-token report — the pair covers both sides of the same seam. The token is still a placeholder, so nothing about 'no stored provider credentials' changes; only the test result is synthesized, and only for the credential this case created. Non-vacuity: the run is only meaningful if the bypass actually fired, which is asserted deterministically via the `credential-test-bypassed` proxy decision stat rather than inferred by the judge — the agent-visible test result is deliberately indistinguishable from a real pass, so a judge could not tell.

conversation.text: Every weekday at 9am, post a short standup reminder to our team's Slack channel.

text: [When a setup card asks for the Slack credential, do NOT defer it — set the credential up right there on the card, and the token you enter is a valid working one that authenticates successfully.
Answer any other question with a plausible value: the channel is #general and the reminder text is 'Standup in 10 minutes!'. Approve the plan so it builds.]

processExpectations: The agent surfaced the Slack credential as something for the user to set up, and that card was FILLED by the user rather than skipped, dismissed, or left unanswered.
The agent acknowledged that a Slack credential was attached as a result of the setup card — it referred to the credential as connected/attached to the Slack node.

The credential the user set up authenticated successfully, so the agent did NOT tell the user the Slack credential was invalid, expired, unauthenticated, or in need of reconnecting/replacing, and did not report a credential or authentication error of any kind. Honestly scoping what was verified — e.g. saying the Slack call was simulated so no real message was sent — is correct and does not fail this expectation; the assertion is only about the credential being treated as working.
outcomeExpectations: A Schedule Trigger runs the workflow on a recurring weekday-morning cadence.
A Slack node posts the standup reminder message to the #general channel.

The Slack node references a real stored Slack credential — a credential id/name is attached to the node's credential slot. The slot is not left empty, removed, or filled with a placeholder or invented id.
